Chapter 5: Coordinating Coherent Action for Real Results
So, you’ve got a clear diagnosis and a strong guiding policy in place. Now comes the most exciting part—turning those ideas into real, meaningful action. This is where strategy steps out of the planning room and starts making a difference in the real world.
But let’s be honest, just doing a lot of things doesn’t guarantee success. Coherent action means making sure every effort fits together, so that each move actually strengthens the others. Picture a rowing team for a moment. If everyone rows in a different direction, the boat just spins in circles. But when the whole crew pulls together, the boat flies across the water.
That’s the kind of alignment organizations need. Every department, every team, and every individual should understand how their work connects to the bigger strategy. When everyone’s on the same page, your guiding policy comes to life—and you start seeing real results.
Now, there are a few key principles for making sure your actions stay coherent:
First, consistency. Every action should reinforce your guiding policy, not work against it. If your focus is on delivering top-notch customer service, then everything—hiring, training, even reward systems—should support that goal.
Next up, prioritization. You can’t do everything at once, so it’s important to decide where to put your energy and resources. Go after the actions that’ll have the biggest impact.
Then there’s sequencing. Some things just need to come first. For example, if you want to wow customers, maybe you have to start by investing in employee training before anything else.
And don’t forget adaptation. Coherence doesn’t mean being stuck in one way of doing things. If the world changes, you may need to tweak your approach—but always keep it aligned with your main strategy.
Let’s make this real with an example. Imagine a manufacturing company that wants to compete on quality, not price. Coherent actions here might look like investing in better materials, tightening quality controls, and teaching employees problem-solving skills. Each step supports the next, and together, they make the strategy much stronger.
But there’s more. Coherent action also means finding those special leverage points—places where a small effort can spark big results. Maybe it’s a unique technology, a trusted brand, or a powerful partnership. If you focus your energy on these hotspots, you can achieve a lot more—without spreading yourself too thin.
And that’s key: don’t try to do too much at once. If you scatter your resources, you lose impact and coherence. It’s smarter to target a few important actions that really move the needle.
Of course, you’ll want to keep an eye on your progress. Coherent action isn’t just a one-and-done thing—it’s an ongoing process. Track your results, learn from what happens, and be ready to adjust as you go. That feedback loop is what keeps your actions lined up with your strategy and your goals.
So, here’s the key takeaway: coherent action is what actually powers your strategy forward. It’s how you turn plans into real outcomes, making sure your team’s efforts are focused, aligned, and truly effective.
